results.resolution: rule 4 (one-way figure a source states) for dist_km; gain_ft from two sources; rule 2 applied to the pins/line so the distances they carry agree with the North Fork Quinault trail the row now describes
results.summary: Mount Seattle's approach is about 19 miles one way up the North Fork Quinault (not the old 61-mile Elwha round trip) with about 5,750 ft of gain; the distance, gain, day-by-day pin mileages and the leftover Elwha wording now all describe that one approach, and the pins and drawn line that followed the Skyline Ridge route instead are removed.
results.evidence: dist_km 98.17 km (61 mi) was the old Elwha round trip. A club route listing states the approach as 19 miles along the North Fork Quinault with 5,750 ft of gain. The park's trail page puts Low Divide 16 miles from the North Fork trailhead (519 ft to 3,602 ft), and an independent 2010 trip report over the same trail agrees (Twelvemile about 11.4 mi from the car, the last 4 miles climbing to Low Divide; out again as 11 miles to Halfway House plus 5 to the car), leaving about 3 miles of climbers' route from Low Divide past Seattle Meadows to the 6,246 ft summit -- consistent with the 19. dist_km set to 30.58 km (19 mi, the stated one-way figure). Gain: 5,750 ft stated by the club listing; the park's elevations give a net 519 -> 3,602 ft to Low Divide plus 2,644 ft on to the summit = 5,727 ft, and the 2010 report measured about 3,100 ft of climbing to Low Divide (-> ~5,750 total), so gain_ft 7,500 (an Elwha-side figure) becomes 5,750. The row mixed two approaches: its day plan, route breakdown, road card and trailhead use the North Fork Quinault river trail, but pins 1-4 (Three Lakes, Kimta Peak, Promise Creek Bench, Beauty Pass) and the drawn line follow the Skyline Ridge primitive route, whose park page gives ~23 miles from Three Lakes to Low Divide on top of the climb to Three Lakes -- which is why the pins put Low Divide at mile 27 and the summit at 30.5. Rule 2: the maintained river trail is the most-documented line in current use, so the Skyline pins are removed, the line is cleared, Low Divide's distMi becomes 16 (two sources), the summit's 19, and Seattle Meadows' distMi is nulled (no source splits the last 3 miles). The Skyline route stays described as an alternative in approach_variants and in the approach prose, whose '16-20 miles one-way' is corrected (the ridge is far longer than 20). The route-breakdown '~3 mi' for Low Divide to Seattle Meadows is dropped because it would put the meadows alone at the full 19 miles. The descent line and crowd estimate still named the Elwha approach and are re-pointed. NOT fixed and worth an owner look: the day plan states miles only for the summit day (4), and lib/outing.js effDistKm prefers the itinerary's day-miles sum over dist_km, so the route page will still show the approach as about 2 mi one way until either the other day plan days carry miles or the reader ignores a partial itinerary.

results.resolution: rule 4: dist_km set to the one-way trailhead-to-camp distance (21 mi) instead of the 45-mile round trip
results.summary: Bear Mountain North Buttress: the one-way approach from Hannegan Pass is about 21 miles to the saddle camp, not 45 (that is the round trip), so the stored distance is halved to match the page's own text.
results.evidence: 72.4 km is the 45-mile round trip (both rows' own text: about 21 miles trailhead-to-camp, 5-6 days and about 45 miles round trip). The trail distance from the Hannegan Pass trailhead down the Chilliwack River trail to the Bear Creek camp is about 17 miles in a climbing-area route guide, and a hiking guide gives the Chilliwack River trail as 17.3 miles one way to its end (the park's trail report says the trail is cleared to Bear Creek camp and abandoned beyond). An independent route write-up of the North Buttress (from the Canadian side, which meets this approach at Bear Creek) puts Bear Creek at about 6 miles and the saddle camp at about 9 miles, i.e. about 3 miles and 4,300 ft from Bear Creek to camp, with the base of the route under a mile beyond. So one-way to camp is about 17 + 3-4 = 21 miles, the figure the row's own approach, pins (camp at mile 21) and day plan (12 + 9 miles) already state; dist_km set to 33.8 km (21 mi). Caveat for the owner: no single source states 21 miles from Hannegan -- the 17-mile trail part is two-sourced, the ~3-4 mile off-trail part rests on one write-up. Halving the 45-mile figure would give nearly the same (22.5) but only the row states that round trip.

results.evidence: dist_km 22.53 km = 14.0 mi, the round trip: the row's own day plan totals 14.5 mi, its summit pin sits at mile 7.3, and a 2018 trip report for the North Peak specifically (out and back from the Saddle Lake / Tupso Pass trailhead via Goat Flats, Tin Can Gap and the col) logs 14 miles round trip and 5,600 ft. A peak page for the 6,870 ft summit (the North Peak's coordinates) gives the trail #641 approach as 16 miles round trip; a hiking guide gives 15 miles round trip to the lookout on the neighbouring south summit, which shares everything to Tin Can Gap. Sources therefore span 7-8 miles one way; 7.5 mi (12.07 km) is set: half the lookout round trip and the midpoint of the two North Peak round trips (14 and 16). Gain (5,600) matches the North Peak report and is unchanged. Owner follow-up, not changed: a hiking guide's current access note says Tupso Pass Road (FR 41) has a washout and a closure well short of the trailhead, open to foot and bike only; the row's road card has no status and its partner notes mention a washout, so the drivable start (and so the real walking distance) should be re-checked.
